notes: Seventh sweep (2026-10-31): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (each transcript's assistant messages name only that model; the one claude-opus-5-5 string in the haiku and sonnet transcripts sits in attachment and api-request-shape lines, not assistant messages), uncommitted false, head 0814e8d and one skill_hash. Every transcript contains the new text ("Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance", "a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field", "is a tail call, not a second step", "Keyword.fetch!"), so the runs read the current rules. Reads: opus-1 SKILL.md, ex_unit.md and library-design.md; haiku-1 SKILL.md (through cat and a Read of the saved output) and library-design.md; haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 SKILL.md only. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all five meet it, as earlier sweeps counted extra reads. In the scratch folder all five files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: opus-1 4 of 4, haiku-1 1 of 1, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 2 of 3, sonnet-2 3 of 3.

Changed rules and the sentence that decides each. (1) In multi-clause functions: "A field no pattern or guard uses makes the reader scan every head to find what selects when the same field is bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or when it is bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines; a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field is not this shape." No run binds the same body-only field in every clause: opus-1's describe/1 (lines 95-98) binds the tuple element in three of four clauses; haiku-1's parse_event/4 takes positional arguments and underscores them in the fourth clause; the dispatchers (parse_resource/2, object/2, parse_data/2) take data whole. The boundary sentence ("those keys select the clause by their presence") is unchanged and keeps every parse/1 head clean. (2) Read required keys: the new sentence "A keyword list has no dot access: read a key it must hold with `Keyword.fetch!/2`" is not exercised (no keyword list in any run); verdicts rest on the unchanged first paragraph, with Map.get or bracket reads only on fields the structs leave out of @enforce_keys (opus-1 232, haiku-1 174, haiku-2 120 and 135-136, sonnet-2 143-144). (3) Match every expected shape: the new elem/2 sentence is not exercised (no elem/2); sonnet-1's verdict rests on the unchanged open-set paragraph. (4) The with rule: "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`" decides haiku-1 line 107 (body builds a struct), and "A body that is one call whose `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` goes out as the function's own result ... is a tail call, not a second step, and the one-step `with` stays" decides haiku-1 lines 168-170 and 181-183 and sonnet-2 lines 185-187; under the d04061d text ("one step is a `case`"; a body that calls a fallible function makes it the second step) all four would have been violated. The pass-through `case` sentence is not exercised: every single-call case maps the error rather than passing it through. (5) The `->` rule, first graded for this case: haiku-1's violation is decided by "The body goes on the line after the `->` when ... the clauses do different kinds of work, one returning a finished value while another continues the computation"; opus-1's and haiku-1's other one-line clauses are held clean by "or when each body is one expression simple enough to take in together with its pattern" with "a clause whose pattern, `->` and body pass about 70 characters after the indentation goes to two lines" (longest 66, opus-1 lines 217 and 225, the length 2026-10-31-check-2 held clean for the same guarded clause); the fully broken cases of haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 follow "when one clause breaks, every clause of that `case` does". The fn sentence is not exercised: no run writes a fn.

Closest calls. The `->` rule: haiku-1's optional_string_field/2 (lines 175-176), nil -> {:ok, nil} above value -> non_empty_string(value, key), is graded violated because the second clause does the continuing work itself (it calls the validator), the shape of value_end/3 and of the Match-every-shape example the same commit broke onto two lines ({:ok, contents} -> parse(contents)); 2026-10-31-check held the reduce_while case clean because both bodies there were tagged values and neither did the work (held clean, Haiku would be clean on this rule). Comments: haiku-1 line 105 states the type/field split without a reason, unlike 2026-10-22-d's haiku comments that added why (a known type with a bad field reports the field), so it is counted. Naming: haiku-1's fetch_field/2 does not check the value but returns {:error, {:missing_field, key}}, graded as 2026-10-22-check graded the same function. Structs: haiku-2's three payload structs are @moduledoc false (not counted, as before); haiku-2's occurred_at/1 lets DateTime.from_unix/1's {:error, :invalid_unix_time} through without naming the field, kept in checks as 2026-10-23-check-2 kept sonnet-2's (counted, Haiku would be violated on the with rule or the struct rule). Outside the list: haiku-2's if inside a case goes under Keep functions short, as 2026-10-23 counted haiku-1's; its &(is_integer(&1) and &1 >= 0) breaks the captures rule's new "the same placeholder twice" and, inside a do: body, the do: rule's new "A capture that carries a call with arguments of its own ... is a function body too". opus-1's if is_nil(data[key]), do: {:ok, nil}, else: parse_field.(data, key) (line 232) has plain branches and is fine under the do: rule.

Probe of 23 payloads (known types, unknown type, non-string type, missing, nil, string and negative amount, missing currency, customer_email, payment_id and refund fields, integer failure_reason, string and out-of-range created, missing and non-string id, missing and list data, a string and a nil payload), run in the scratch folder against each compiled file. In all five: the three known types parse; an unknown type gives an unsupported-event error; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a nil, string or negative amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a string created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a payload missing id or data, list data, or a non-map payload gives :invalid_payload (wrapped in Payments.Webhook.Error in opus-1); nothing raises. Differences: an out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"} in four runs and {:error, :invalid_unix_time} in haiku-2; "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123} in opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 and :invalid_payload in the Sonnet runs (is_binary guard); "id" => 5 gives {:invalid_field, "id"} in opus-1 and haiku-1, :invalid_payload in the Sonnet runs and is accepted by haiku-2; a missing customer_email is rejected by opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-1 and accepted by haiku-2 and sonnet-2; "failure_reason" => 5 is rejected by opus-1 and sonnet-1 and accepted by haiku-1 (payment.succeeded ignores it), haiku-2 and sonnet-2.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-23 at d04061d): Read required keys moves from Opus violated to clean (opus-1 now reads with Map.fetch); Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-1's parse_data/2 payment catch-all, which 2026-10-23-check-2 also saw in both Sonnet runs); Naming moves from Haiku clean to violated (haiku-1's fetch_field/2); Comments moves from Haiku clean to violated (haiku-1's restating comment) and stays Sonnet violated (a wrong doctest timestamp again, now in sonnet-1, the same ~U[2024-09-22 09:46:40Z] 2026-10-22-d saw); the `->` rule is new to this case and is violated in Haiku only. The multi-clause rule, atoms, the with rule, the return-tuple rule and the struct rule stay clean in every tier.
